transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-15
Time: 09:00 PT / 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Sarah Lee (BrightCare CTO), Tom Nguyen (BrightCare ML Ops), Emily Park (BrightCare Platform)
Shared links: model-catalog-deck.pdf, redwood-security-overview.pdf, benchmark-template.xlsx

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm jordan with redwood inference, i'm the ae on the account. um quick intro, diego is our solutions engineer who will run the demo, and we'll walk through the model catalog, the console, and the optimize suggestions.
[00:12] Sarah: hi jordan, thanks. quick note, i'm on in the office with tom and emily. we're primarily evaluating model options for our triage assistant and patient communication flows. latency and PHI handling are our top concerns.
[00:25] Jordan: totally, that's exactly what we'll focus on. diego, want to kick off?
[00:28] Diego: yeah sure, quick screen share — i'm pulling up the redwood console. heads up the auto transcript sometimes calls it redwood catlog or redwood dedicated as "redwood dedicate" so ignore that if you see it.
[00:40] [screen share noises]
[00:45] Diego: okay so this is the model catalog — we surface curated open models and we surface performance profiles next to each model: throughput, per-token latency, memory footprint, compatibility flags (quantization friendly, kv-cache support, hf-compat). you can filter by task (chat, generation, embeddings), cost tier, and hardware target.
[01:10] Tom: can you show an example for a 2k token prompt workload? our triage prompts average 1.6k tokens.
[01:17] Diego: sure — i'll apply the 2k filter and two model families come up: a quant-optim LLaMA-2 variant and a mosaic/llmfusion-derived model. see here — the compatibility matrix column shows whether the model supports int8 quant, bf16 kernels, and multi-gpu KV cache. note the estimated p95 latency is measured on our dedicated gpus and on our hosted fleet — there's a dropdown to compare region/hardware.
[01:45] Emily: the numbers seem optimistic — are those measured or simulated?
[01:49] Diego: good question. the catalog pulls from our benchmark corpus and the benchmark spreadsheet we ran in lab. the score shows lab-measured p50/p95 with our standard prompt set and config; we also surface a confidence band and the test harness link.
[02:05] Sarah: and if we want to run on-prem or in our VPC, do those numbers still apply?
[02:09] Diego: they'll be close if you use similar GPU types. for private deployments we provide a compatibility matrix that maps model variants to recommended kernel configs and quantization profiles. you can export that matrix as CSV to feed into your internal validation.
[02:22] Jordan: also worth noting — in the console under model details there's a "deployment compatibility" tab which lists known-good driver/kernel combos and a notes section where we call out special considerations e.g., sequence-length optimizations or kv-cache sizing.
[02:35] [00:150 mis-typing in transcript]
[02:38] Tom: talking about cost, can the console show cost per 1k tokens for each profile?
[02:42] Diego: yes — that's part of the Optimize panel. i'll switch to Optimize — here we show batching suggestions, cache TTLs, and a cost estimate for each model+config. for example the quantized LLaMA-2 variant drops per-token compute by ~40% compared to baseline, but you need to trade off slight quality delta. we also show an estimated latency delta if you enable larger batch sizes.
[03:10] Sarah: how do you track quality regressions if we change quantization?
[03:14] Diego: we tie quality monitoring to eval sets — you can upload a prompt set (we have a sample spreadsheet) and Redwood will run A/B comparisons and push regression alerts. that's in the Optimize -> Quality tab.
[03:25] Emily: is the A/B run automated or do we need to engineer it?
[03:28] Diego: both options — we have automated runs in hosted and tooling for private where you can run the harness locally. i'll link the benchmark-template.xlsx.
[03:36] [03:40 short cross talk]
[03:40] Jordan: let's demo the API briefly — diego, can you switch to the API playground?
[03:44] Diego: yep, this is the REST playground. you can select model variant, set max_tokens, temperature, and enable streaming. watch the request — we're hitting /v1/generate with model=redwood-llama2-q8 and we get streaming tokens back. note the sdk call is two lines in python in the snippet.
[04:05] Tom: do you support tool-calling and structured output?
[04:07] Diego: yes — tool-calling is supported and the catalog tags models that have stable structured output behavior in our tests. the table has a "structured-output" flag. some open models need mild instruction tuning for reliable JSON output.
[04:19] Sarah: any gotchas around long-run KV cache size? our workflows re-use context across sessions.
[04:24] Diego: the runtime supports persistent KV caching and we show recommended cache TTLs per model. for models with large past-context we recommend explicit cache pruning and we provide metrics in the console for cache hit-rates.
[04:35] Emily: security — SSO, audit logs, data residency — quickly?
[04:38] Jordan: for hosted API we have SOC2 and infra-level audit logs, single-tenant dedicated gets you stronger isolation and private has the on-prem control plane. we support SAML/SSO, RBAC, and KMS integration for encryption at rest. i'll drop the redwood-security-overview.pdf after the call.
[04:56] Sarah: are there customers who have done PHI workloads on hosted?
[05:00] Jordan: most PHI workloads go dedicated or private; we have a few enterprise customers that run HIPAA workflows on dedicated capacity with contractual BAAs — we can connect you to a reference.
[05:12] Tom: awesome — what about fallback policies? like if dedicated capacity spikes, can requests route to hosted cheaper models?
[05:18] Diego: yes — smart routing supports policy-based fallbacks (by latency, cost, region, or model-family). the console has a policy editor to set thresholds; when capacity is constrained the runtime will route to preapproved variants with graceful degradation.
[05:32] [05:35 small pause]
[05:36] Sarah: okay so practical ask — we want a short pilot on dedicated for 2 weeks with our 10k prompt set to validate p95 latency and token cost. what's the typical timeline?
[05:45] Jordan: timeline depends on infra but typical is 2-4 weeks to spin up reserved capacity and run the benchmark. diego, what do you need from them to run the bench?
[05:53] Diego: sample prompts, desired latency SLO, and preferred GPU SKU. i'll send the infra checklist and the benchmark harness. we'll provision a small dedicated pool and run both quantized and fp16 runs to compare.
[06:05] Tom: for pricing, do you have an estimate for a 1 month pilot?
[06:08] Jordan: i'll follow up with a formal pilot quote — rough estimate will be in the pricing sheet i'll send, depends on hours and reserved vs burst capacity.
[06:15] Emily: one more — compatibility matrix export: can we pull a CSV with all driver/kernel combos recommended?
[06:20] Diego: yes, export button in the deployment compatibility tab, and it includes recommended NCCL/driver versions and notes.
[06:28] [06:30 brief overlap]
[06:30] Sarah: any extension around observability — traces per request?
[06:33] Diego: we emit tracing hooks and per-token latency metrics. console shows token-level breakdown and route traces, and you can stream logs to your SIEM via our integrations.
[06:44] Jordan: quick recap — action items: jordan sends pricing and model catalog PDF; diego shares benchmark harness and infra checklist; brightcare shares prompt set and SLOs; schedule pilot kickoff. everyone ok?
[06:56] Sarah: yes, that works. appreciate the demo.
[07:00] Jordan: great — we'll follow up by end of week with the docs and next steps. thanks all.

Notes about transcript: occasional transcription errors (e.g., "redwood dedicate" instead of "Redwood Dedicated", "llama two" sometimes spelled out). The technical details (kernel versions, KV cache sizing) were high level; deeper SE follow-up planned.
